claims.text: The baseline coating is an equiatomic or near-equiatomic homogeneous FeNiCrCoCu thin coating on a conventional metal substrate.
The baseline coating is annealed at 700°C.
Raising the annealing temperature from 700°C to 750°C for 30 minutes in an inert atmosphere produces a more refined nanocrystalline grain structure.
The elevated-temperature anneal increases the density of grain boundaries.
The refined microstructure enhances grain-boundary mobility.
Enhanced grain-boundary mobility facilitates dynamic recrystallization during high-temperature sliding.
Dynamic recrystallization distributes deformation more uniformly.
Dynamic recrystallization impedes the initiation and propagation of wear-causing cracks or shear bands.
Relative to the 700°C baseline, the coating annealed at 750°C will have reduced wear volume during high-temperature sliding.
Relative to the 700°C baseline, the coating annealed at 750°C will have a lower friction coefficient.
Relative to the 700°C baseline, the coating annealed at 750°C will exhibit more evidence of dynamic recrystallization after sliding.
The coating annealed at 750°C will exhibit a finer and more uniform post-test grain structure.
The coating annealed at 750°C will undergo moderated microscopic deformation during sliding.
The predictions apply when sliding temperature is high enough to activate grain-boundary processes and dynamic recrystallization.
The predictions apply only below conditions causing excessive oxidation or melting of the coating.
The magnitude of the wear and deformation changes may depend on coating thickness, substrate interaction, and sliding conditions.
